title: Why do stars twinkle?
examples: Teacher, why do stars look like they are dancing?
What makes the stars twinkle when we look at them?
Is it the stars themselves that are twinkling?

explain.say: Some students wonder why stars seem to twinkle at night.
The air around Earth is not always still and calm.
These moving air layers bend the light coming from the stars.
When the light bends, it makes the star look like it is wiggling.
A real-life example is looking at a distant boat on the water.

draw.text: Hot air bends light from objects.

explain.say: The most common mistake is thinking the stars are actually blinking.

draw.text: Stars do not blink on their own.

faq.q: Do stars twinkle all the time?
faq.a: Stars twinkle more when the air is moving a lot. If the air is very still, the twinkling is much less noticeable.
asks: Why do they twinkle when it is windy?

faq.q: Is the twinkling because the stars are moving?
faq.a: No, the stars are very far away and do not move enough for us to see that way. The twinkling is caused by Earth's air.

faq.q: Does the Moon twinkle like the stars?
faq.a: The Moon does not twinkle as much as the stars do. Because it is closer, its light is steadier to our eyes.

faq.q: What is the air that bends the light called?
faq.a: The air that bends the light is part of Earth's atmosphere. The atmosphere is the blanket of air around our planet.

faq.q: Does this happen with all lights?
faq.a: It happens with any light coming from a very far source. A light source that is close to you will not show this twinkling effect.

facts: Stars are extremely far away from Earth.
The Earth's atmosphere is made of moving air.
This moving air bends the light rays coming from stars.
This bending makes the stars appear to twinkle.

quiz.say: What causes the twinkling effect of stars?
quiz.why: The atmosphere is the layer of air that bends the light coming from the stars.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the stars are too far away to actually blink.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the Moon is much closer and its light is steadier.
wrong.2: This is wrong because clouds block light, they do not bend it to make it twinkle.

quiz.say: If the air is very still, how will the stars look?
quiz.why: When the air is calm, there are fewer layers to bend the light, so the stars look steady.

wrong.0: Twinkling only happens when the air is moving and bending the light.
wrong.1: Fading means the light is getting weaker, but the air movement causes wiggling.
wrong.2: The stars do not disappear just because the air is calm.

quiz.say: When looking at a distant object, what is bending the light?
quiz.why: The layers of air in the atmosphere are constantly moving and bending the light path.

wrong.0: The object itself is not changing; it is the light reaching us that is bent.
wrong.1: Our eyes are fine; the problem is with the light traveling through the air.
wrong.2: The stars' actual brightness does not change; the path to us changes.
